summary: Nicola Bajetta is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Bajetta studied as a doctoral local researcher and worked as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg (both attested 2026).

Nicola Di Cosmo is a historian of Sinology and Central Asia who studied at Indiana State and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD 1991). He held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, Canterbury, Columbia, and as Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the IAS (~2003).

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held positions at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1902–1903). He held a post at Leiden University starting in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and held a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University, under supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, and teachers Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, and U-tain Wongsathit. He was attested at Thammasat University in 2016.

Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010; attested as former assistant professor in 2026).

Nicolas Tournadre is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle under Claude Hagège. He held posts at CNRS, INALCO, Paris 8, University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University, alongside affiliations with Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and LACITO.
Nicole Baden is a specialist in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (~1958–1976) and was professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO/École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1966–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen as lektor (1844), full professor (1850), and rektor (1867–1868).

Nigel Allan is a scholar of history and archaeology who succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Ananda Mohan, Murari Chand, Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden, he served as Calcutta University's Chief Librarian and Bageswari Professor, and later directed the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Jovic studied under teacher Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008) and completed a Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

Nikolai Solmsdorf is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and Alexander von Rospatt. He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nikolai Trubetzkoy (1890–1938) was a linguist who studied at Moscow University (~1908–1913) and under August Leskien (~1913–1914). He held academic posts at Sofia University (~1920–1922) and the University of Vienna (~1922–1938).

Nile Green is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Manchester (~2004–2007) and serves as Professor and Ibn Khaldun Endowed Chair in World History at UCLA (~2007).
Nima Repper is an Indology scholar who studied at and served as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who founded the Indology Graduate Seminar in 2008. She has held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher educated at Glasgow and Oxford. He held chairs and posts at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University (1967–1982), UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998), and UC Berkeley (1976–1998).
